chapter: Will Vodery and the road shows
title: Will Vodery as bandmaster, and Whaley playing flute and piccolo
summary: He met Vodery as Army bandmaster in 1918 and learned flute and piccolo from a Frenchman to fill a gap.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: That was the era. Now, you wanted to talk about -- I wanted to get back to some of the things in the '30s and the '20s that was very important to you. And we haven't spoken too much about it. We spoke of it gradually last time. But go ahead and talk about Will Vodery, which I know you admired.
Oh, yeah. I met Bill Vodery here in New York, when I went in the Army in 1918, he was bandmaster.
And I wasn't in the band at the time, I was in headquarters' company. When I got transferred to the band, and Vodery was the bandmaster. And he used to rehearse us, and you know what I played?
Yeah, I took up every instrument. They had enough but they didn't have no flute player, no piccolo player. So I had a French man there, and he taught me the flute.
Wow, I didn't know Tom Whaley was a flute player.
Yeah, I used to go out when they had parades and I'd play the piccolo. Man, I'd get a headache, I was walking like I was drunk, playing that flute. But, yeah, I --
